answer: Each agent identity binds to a nonce-chained work history: every completed task appends a signed, hash-chained record, like coral building a reef where each polyp cements onto the last. Verifiers accept only chains anchored to one genesis kernel, so an identity cannot fork into parallel copies - any branch reuses a nonce and both branches are voided. The mesa of earned reputation is non-duplicable: a sybil attacker must redo every task from scratch at full compute and payment cost, while fresh clones start with zero history and earn nothing.
